title: The SYSK Holiday Spectacular
summary: Christmas special of Stuff You Should Know covering four loosely linked holiday topics: the theory that Santa Claus was inspired by Siberian/Sami shamans and the fly agaric (Amanita muscaria) mushroom; the copyright history of Frank Capra's It's a Wonderful Life, which entered the public domain and became a TV marathon staple; the origins and copyright fight over "Santa Claus Is Coming to Town" by Haven Gillespie and J. Fred Coots; the history and process of Christmas tree flocking (fake snow); and the centuries-old Declaration of Christmas Peace read in Turku, Finland. The episode ends with the hosts' holiday wishes and a reading of the declaration.
topics: Santa Claus Is Coming to Town

entities.name: Santa Claus Is Coming to Town

segments.title: Opening banter and holiday setup
segments.summary: The hosts open the Christmas special, note it is released ad-free, and banter about the episode's lineup and the content warning for kids.

segments.title: Santa Claus and psychedelic mushrooms
segments.summary: The hosts discuss a theory, drawing on a Mental Floss-style article and a Sierra College professor's research, that Santa Claus was inspired by Sami/Siberian shamans who gave dried fly agaric mushrooms as winter solstice gifts, dressed in red and white, and came down smoke holes. They also note reindeer eat the mushrooms and urine can be used to detoxify them.

segments.title: It's a Wonderful Life: flop, public domain, and copyright
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the 1946 film It's a Wonderful Life, directed by Frank Capra and released by Liberty Films, which flopped initially, over-budgeted, and entered the public domain in 1994 after a copyright renewal lapse. Its TV marathon popularity followed, until the Stewart v. Abend ruling and NBC's later rights acquisition ended the marathons. Josh pushes Chuck to watch it.

segments.title: Santa Claus Is Coming to Town: songwriters and copyright
segments.summary: The hosts describe Haven Gillespie and J. Fred Coots writing the song at Leo Feist's request, Eddie Cantor's popularization of it, its strong early sheet music sales, and a copyright termination dispute with E.M.I. that a court resolved in favor of the Coots family in 2016.
topics: Santa Claus Is Coming to Town

segments.title: Brief transition and Christmas music tangent
segments.summary: Short transition between segments with a brief tangent about animatronic bands and a documentary about Showbiz Pizza.

segments.title: Christmas tree flocking
segments.summary: Based on a Mental Floss article, the hosts explain flocking as artificial snow applied to Christmas trees, its history including a 1800s recipe and a General Mills Snow Flock kit, the modern process by Peak Seasons using a flock gun and water mist, and a DIY recipe. They also discuss tree netting for transport.

segments.title: Declaration of Christmas Peace in Turku, Finland
segments.summary: The hosts describe Turku, Finland's annual Declaration of Christmas Peace, read from a balcony after the cathedral bells toll at midday on Christmas Eve. It bans violence and work over the holiday, with historically severe fines, and the punishment was removed from law in the 1970s though the reading continues.

segments.title: Holiday wishes and closing declaration
segments.summary: The hosts wish listeners happy holidays, encourage kindness during a hard season, and close by reading the Declaration of Christmas Peace in full.
